items.evidence: The e2e 'the side-pot result keeps Hand over on one line...' passes in Chromium and WebKit. The test reads Range client-rect tops for the title, per-span line counts, scrollWidth<=clientWidth, list width >= half the content width, right edge/page width <= 1280 and axe, and attaches both screenshots. Holdout at 1280 and 1024 wide, both scenes, both browsers: block flex-direction column; title 1 line; each list starts below the previous row; lists 974 px wide of 974 px content; items 42 px tall with no overflow; docW <= viewport. Screenshots viewed: readable. Note: the test strength is confirmed by reading only, plus the builder's red check. I did not run the test against the old CSS.

The e2e 'a single-pot result stays on one row' passes in both browsers, using a vertical-overlap check between the title and Winners boxes. Holdout: in the shown-hands scene the block has flex-direction row, the title is 1 line, and every list sits to the right of the title. The render output still contains the exact '

Hand over

' and no Pot winners list.

tests/ui/split-side-pot.acceptance.test.tsx passes in the full npm test run. It asserts the exact item texts, and equality to pots[k].text/potText/winnersText for both the split and SIDE_POT_SHOWDOWN scenes. Holdout render of a crafted three-pot table (one pot split): the li texts equal the VM texts 'Main pot $60 · You win $60', 'Side pot 1 $40 · Ben wins $40' and 'Side pot 2 $81 · Ben wins $41, Ava wins $40'.

The e2e 'a split side pot reads ...' passes in Chromium and WebKit. It checks the exact two list-item texts with toHaveText and that there are no http(s) requests. Holdout browser read of the split scene gives the same two texts.

The unit 'pot result text is built from potText and winnersText' passes. The existing toEqual includes potText/winnersText 'Main pot $60'/'You win $60' and 'Side pot $80'/'Ben wins $80'. The awk|grep -c 'join(' check on HandResult returns 0. Holdout unit: the split VM gives the exact potText/winnersText/text triples.

The e2e 'game-type options keep the same height...' passes in both browsers. The test asserts equal heights in every reading and >= 44 px for Game type and Line-up. Holdout against the built preview, with arrow-key selection cycling both groups in both browsers: the only height observed was 44 px.
